patterns.usage_note: Volitional form plus が: a concessive that brushes the preceding condition aside as irrelevant, often with a curt, washing-my-hands tone, and typically stronger and more emphatic than 〜ても, which it beats precisely when the condition is being declared beside the point in advance rather than genuinely weighed as a live possibility. It is almost always interchangeable with 〜(よ)うと, though 〜(よ)うと is the more neutral, written-leaning member of the pair and 〜うが the more emphatic one, most at home in the paired frames (〜うが〜うが, 〜うが〜まいが). The corpus rule licenses only verbs and い-adjectives here (行こうが, 高かろうが); nouns and な-adjectives take the same construction through the copula (学生だろうが, 下手だろうが).

examples.ruby: 指[ゆび]がどれだけ震[ふる]えようが、祖父[そふ]は毎日[まいにち]筆[ふで]を握[にぎ]る。
examples.english: No matter how badly his fingers shake, my grandfather picks up his brush every day.

examples.ruby: どんなに値段[ねだん]が高[たか]かろうが、兄[あに]はあの時計[とけい]を買[か]うつもりらしい。
examples.english: However expensive it is, my brother apparently means to buy that watch.

examples.ruby: 雨[あめ]が降[ふ]ろうが雪[ゆき]が降[ふ]ろうが、大会[たいかい]は予定[よてい]どおり行[おこな]われる。
examples.english: Rain or snow, the tournament goes ahead as scheduled.

patterns.usage_note: A rhetorical question that presses a judgment the speaker treats as obvious onto the hearer; in this class the typical color is reproach or complaint, though the same form also carries admiration (いい店じゃないか). Bare 〜じゃない with rising intonation is the gender-neutral everyday equivalent and the one most speakers actually say; adding か is what makes it blunt and masculine-sounding, じゃないですか is the polite version and often just softens an assertion, ではないか is written or formal, and じゃねえか is rough speech. Note that after a volitional (行こうじゃないか) it stops being a rhetorical question and becomes an invitation, a separate function.

examples.ruby: 昨日[きのう]ちゃんと確認[かくにん]すると言[い]ったじゃないか。
examples.english: You told me yesterday you'd double-check it, didn't you!

examples.ruby: そんなに怒[おこ]らなくても、あの子[こ]はまだ子供[こども]じゃないか。
examples.english: Go easy on her; she's still just a kid, come on.

examples.ruby: ほら、あの雲[くも]、犬[いぬ]の形[かたち]をしているじゃないですか。
examples.english: Look — that cloud, it's shaped like a dog, isn't it?
